sanskrit: adhītyāpi hi yo vedān nyāyavidbhyaḥ prayacchati gurukarmapraśaṃsī ca so 'pi svarge mahīyate
english: And he who, having mastered the Vedas, imparts them to those versed in right reasoning, and who extols the duty owed to a teacher—he too is exalted in heaven.

sanskrit: kṣatriyo 'dhyayane yukto yajane dānakarmaṇi yuddhe yaś ca paritrātā so 'pi svarge mahīyate
english: The kṣatriya devoted to study, to sacrifice, and to the work of giving, who is a protector in battle—he too is exalted in heaven.

sanskrit: vaiśyaḥ svakarmanirataḥ pradānāl labhate mahat śūdraḥ svakarmanirataḥ svargaṃ śuśrūṣayārcchati
english: The vaiśya intent upon his own duty gains a great reward through giving; the śūdra intent upon his own duty attains heaven through dutiful service.

sanskrit: śūrā bahuvidhāḥ proktās teṣām arthāṃś ca me śṛṇu śūrānvayānāṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ phalaṃ śūrasya caiva ha
english: Heroes have been declared to be of many kinds; hear from me their meanings, and the reward set forth for those of heroic lineage and for the hero himself.

sanskrit: yajñaśūrā dame śūrāḥ satyaśūrās tathāpare yuddhaśūrās tathaivoktā dānaśūrāś ca mānavāḥ
english: There are heroes in sacrifice, heroes in self-restraint, and others who are heroes in truth; men called heroes in battle, and likewise heroes in giving.

sanskrit: buddhiśūrās tathaivānye kṣamāśūrās tathāpare ārjave ca tathā śūrāḥ śame vartanti mānavāḥ
english: Others again are heroes in wisdom, and some heroes in forbearance; and there are men who are heroes in uprightness and who abide in tranquillity.

sanskrit: tais tais tu niyamaiḥ śūrā bahavaḥ santi cāpare vedādhyayanaśūrāś ca śūrāś cādhyāpane ratāḥ
english: By this or that observance there are many other heroes besides: heroes in the study of the Vedas, and heroes devoted to teaching them.

sanskrit: guruśuśrūṣayā śūrāḥ pitṛśuśrūṣayāpare mātṛśuśrūṣayā śūrā bhaikṣyaśūrās tathāpare
english: Heroes in serving the teacher, others in serving the father, heroes in serving the mother, and others again heroes in the life of mendicancy.

sanskrit: sāṃkhyaśūrāś ca bahavo yogaśūrās tathāpare araṇye gṛhavāse ca śūrāś cātithipūjane sarve yānti parāṃl lokān svakarmaphalanirjitān
english: Many are heroes in Sāṃkhya and others heroes in Yoga; heroes in the forest, in the household life, and in the honouring of guests—all of them attain the highest worlds, won by the fruit of their own works.

sanskrit: dhāraṇaṃ sarvavedānāṃ sarvatīrthāvagāhanam satyaṃ ca bruvato nityaṃ samaṃ vā syān na vā samam
english: The retaining of all the Vedas, the bathing at every sacred ford—whether for him who ever speaks the truth these be equal or not equal.

sanskrit: aśvamedhasahasraṃ ca satyaṃ ca tulayā dhṛtam aśvamedhasahasrād dhi satyam eva viśiṣyate
english: A thousand horse-sacrifices and truth were weighed in the balance: truth alone outweighs a thousand horse-sacrifices.

sanskrit: satyena sūryas tapati satyenāgniḥ pradīpyate satyena māruto vāti sarvaṃ satye pratiṣṭhitam
english: By truth the Sūrya gives heat, by truth Agni blazes, by truth the wind blows; all things are established upon truth.

sanskrit: satyena devān prīṇāti pitṝn vai brāhmaṇāṃs tathā satyam āhuḥ paraṃ dharmaṃ tasmāt satyaṃ na laṅghayet
english: By truth one gladdens the gods, the ancestors, and the brāhmaṇas alike. Truth, they say, is the supreme dharma; therefore one should never transgress the truth.

sanskrit: munayaḥ satyaniratā munayaḥ satyavikramāḥ munayaḥ satyaśapathās tasmāt satyaṃ viśiṣyate satyavantaḥ svargaloke modante bharatarṣabha
english: The sages are devoted to truth, the sages have truth for their valour, the sages have truth for their vow; therefore truth is supreme. The truthful rejoice in the world of heaven, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: damaḥ satyaphalāvāptir uktā sarvātmanā mayā asaṃśayaṃ vinītātmā sarvaḥ svarge mahīyate
english: The attainment of the fruit of self-restraint and of truth has been told by me with all my heart. Beyond doubt, every man of disciplined self is exalted in heaven.

sanskrit: brahmacaryasya tu guṇāñ śṛṇu me vasudhādhipa ā janmamaraṇād yas tu brahmacārī bhaved iha na tasya kiṃ cid aprāpyam iti viddhi janādhipa
english: Now hear from me the virtues of chastity, O lord of the earth. He who in this world remains a celibate from birth until death—know, O lord of men, that for him there is nothing unattainable.

sanskrit: bahvyaḥ koṭyas tv ṛṣīṇāṃ tu brahmaloke vasanty uta satye ratānāṃ satataṃ dāntānām ūrdhvaretasām
english: Many tens of millions of seers dwell in the world of Brahmā—those ever delighting in truth, the self-restrained, the keepers of upward-flowing seed.

sanskrit: brahmacaryaṃ dahed rājan sarvapāpāny upāsitam brāhmaṇena viśeṣeṇa brāhmaṇo hy agnir ucyate
english: Chastity, when cultivated, burns away all sins, O king—especially when cultivated by a brāhmaṇa; for the brāhmaṇa is called a very fire.

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ ca tavāpy etad brāhmaṇeṣu tapasviṣu bibheti hi yathā śakro brahmacāripradharṣitaḥ tad brahmacaryasya phalam ṛṣīṇām iha dṛśyate
english: This too is plain to your own eyes among the brāhmaṇas and the ascetics: how Śakra trembles when assailed by a celibate. Such is the fruit of chastity seen here among the seers.

sanskrit: mātāpitroḥ pūjane yo dharmas tam api me śṛṇu śuśrūṣate yaḥ pitaraṃ na cāsūyet kathaṃ cana mātaraṃ vānahaṃvādī gurum ācāryam eva ca
english: Hear from me too the duty that lies in honouring mother and father. He who serves his father and never in any way speaks ill of his mother, who utters no proud word against his elder or his teacher—

sanskrit: tasya rājan phalaṃ viddhi svarloke sthānam uttamam na ca paśyeta narakaṃ guruśuśrūṣur ātmavān
english: —know, O king, that his reward is the highest station in the world of heaven; the self-possessed man who serves his elders shall never behold hell.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca vidhiṃ gavāṃ param ahaṃ śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ yena tāñ śāśvatāṃl lokān akhilān aśnuvīmahi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I wish to hear truly the supreme ordinance concerning cows, by which we may attain in their entirety those everlasting worlds.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca na godānāt paraṃ kiṃ cid vidyate vasudhādhipa gaur hi nyāyāgatā dattā sadyas tārayate kulam
english: Bhīṣma said: There is nothing higher than the gift of a cow, O lord of the earth; for a cow righteously obtained and given away delivers one's whole line at once.

sanskrit: satām arthe samyag utpādito yaḥ; sa vai kḷptaḥ samyag iṣṭaḥ prajābhyaḥ tasmāt pūrvaṃ hy ādikāle pravṛttaṃ; gavāṃ dāne śṛṇu rājan vidhiṃ me
english: That which was rightly created for the good, fashioned aright and consecrated for the welfare of creatures—since the gift of cows has been in practice from the very first beginning, hear from me, O king, its ordinance.

sanskrit: purā goṣūpanītāsu goṣu saṃdigdhadarśinā māndhātrā prakṛtaṃ praśnaṃ bṛhaspatir abhāṣata
english: Of old, when cows had been brought near, Bṛhaspati answered the question put to him by Māndhātṛ, who was in doubt as to what he should behold.

sanskrit: dvijātim abhisatkṛtya śvaḥ kālam abhivedya ca pradānārthe niyuñjīta rohiṇīṃ niyatavrataḥ
english: Having honoured the twice-born and having announced the time on the morrow, the man of steadfast vow should set apart a red cow for the purpose of the gift.

sanskrit: āhvānaṃ ca prayuñjīta samaṅge bahuleti ca praviśya ca gavāṃ madhyam imāṃ śrutim udāharet
english: He should employ the call, 'O perfect-limbed one, O abundant one,' and entering into the midst of the cows he should recite this sacred utterance:

sanskrit: gaur me mātā govṛṣabhaḥ pitā me; divaṃ śarma jagatī me pratiṣṭhā prapadyaivaṃ śarvarīm uṣya goṣu; munir vāṇīm utsṛjed gopradāne
english: 'The cow is my mother, the bull is my father; heaven is my shelter, the earth my support.' Taking refuge thus and passing the night among the cows, the silent one should let forth this speech at the giving of cows.

sanskrit: sa tām ekāṃ niśāṃ gobhiḥ samasakhyaḥ samavrataḥ aikātmyagamanāt sadyaḥ kalmaṣād vipramucyate
english: That man, for that one night a fellow and a vow-sharer of the cows, by reaching oneness with them is at once wholly freed from sin.

sanskrit: utsṛṣṭavṛṣavatsā hi pradeyā sūryadarśane trividhaṃ pratipattavyam arthavādāśiṣaḥ stavāḥ
english: A cow whose bull and calf have been set free is to be given at the sight of the sun; and a threefold formula is to be observed—the explanatory praise, the benediction, and the hymns of laud.

sanskrit: ūrjasvinya ūrjamedhāś ca yajño; garbho 'mṛtasya jagataś ca pratiṣṭhā kṣitau rādhaḥprabhavaḥ śaśvad eva; prājāpatyāḥ sarvam ity arthavādaḥ
english: 'Rich in vigour and full of nourishing strength, they are the sacrifice, the womb of the nectar, and the support of the world; the source of prosperity upon the earth forever, born of Prajāpati'—such is the explanatory praise, comprising all.

sanskrit: gāvo mamainaḥ praṇudantu sauryās; tathā saumyāḥ svargayānāya santu āmnātā me dadatīr āśrayaṃ tu; tathānuktāḥ santu sarvāśiṣo me
english: 'May these cows of the Sun drive away my sin, and may those of the Moon be for my journey to heaven; let those that are named grant me their shelter, and let all those unnamed be a blessing upon me.'

sanskrit: śeṣotsarge karmabhir dehamokṣe; sarasvatyaḥ śreyasi saṃpravṛttāḥ yūyaṃ nityaṃ puṇyakarmopavāhyā; diśadhvaṃ me gatim iṣṭāṃ prapannāḥ
english: 'At the giving away of all that remains, at the releasing of the body through rites, you Sarasvatī-cows are ever set toward the highest good; ever to be carried forth by holy works, grant me, you that have come, the goal I desire.'

sanskrit: yā vai yūyaṃ so 'ham adyaikabhāvo; yuṣmān dattvā cāham ātmapradātā manaścyutā manaevopapannāḥ; saṃdhukṣadhvaṃ saumyarūpograrūpāḥ
english: 'What you are, that am I—today of one single being; in giving you away I give my very self. Released from the mind yet endowed with mind, kindle me, O you of gentle form and terrible form.'

sanskrit: evaṃ tasyāgre pūrvam ardhaṃ vadeta; gavāṃ dātā vidhivat pūrvadṛṣṭam pratibrūyāc cheṣam ardhaṃ dvijātiḥ; pratigṛhṇan vai gopradāne vidhijñaḥ
english: Thus, before him, the giver of cows should first speak the former half according to ordinance, as seen of old; and the twice-born one who knows the rite, in receiving at the gift of cows, should answer with the remaining half.

sanskrit: gāṃ dadānīti vaktavyam arghyavastravasupradaḥ ūdhasyā bharitavyā ca vaiṣṇavīti ca codayet
english: 'I give the cow'—so should it be said by him who bestows the welcome-offering, garments, and wealth; the udder is to be kept filled, and he should declare her sacred to Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: nāma saṃkīrtayet tasyā yathāsaṃkhyottaraṃ sa vai phalaṃ ṣaḍviṃśad aṣṭau ca sahasrāṇi ca viṃśatiḥ
english: He should proclaim her name, and reward upon reward accrues in order of number—twenty-six, and eight, and twenty thousand.

sanskrit: evam etān guṇān vṛddhān gavādīnāṃ yathākramam gopradātā samāpnoti samastān aṣṭame krame
english: Thus the giver of cows wins all these growing merits of cows and the rest, in due order, complete at the eighth stage.

sanskrit: godaḥ śīlī nirbhayaś cārghadātā; na syād duḥkhī vasudātā ca kāmī ūdhasyoḍhā bhārata yaś ca vidvān; vyākhyātās te vaiṣṇavāś candralokāḥ
english: The giver of cows becomes virtuous; the giver of the welcome-offering becomes fearless; the giver of wealth ceases to be sorrowful and gains his desires; and the learned man who has borne the filled udder, O Bhārata—for all these the worlds of Viṣṇu and of the Moon are declared.

sanskrit: gā vai dattvā govratī syāt trirātraṃ; niśāṃ caikāṃ saṃvaseteha tābhiḥ kāmyāṣṭamyāṃ vartitavyaṃ trirātraṃ; rasair vā goḥ śakṛtā prasnavair vā
english: Having given cows, one should keep the cow-vow for three nights, and dwell here for one night among them; on the eighth day, sought of desire, one should pass three nights subsisting on the cow's juices, or on its dung, or on its milk.

sanskrit: vedavratī syād vṛṣabhapradātā; vedāvāptir goyugasya pradāne tathā gavāṃ vidhim āsādya yajvā; lokān agryān vindate nāvidhijñaḥ
english: The giver of a bull becomes a keeper of the Veda-vow; in the gift of a yoke of oxen lies the attainment of the Veda. So the sacrificer who follows the ordinance of cows wins the foremost worlds—but not he who knows not the rite.

sanskrit: kāmān sarvān pārthivān ekasaṃsthān; yo vai dadyāt kāmadughāṃ ca dhenum samyak tāḥ syur havyakavyaughavatyas; tāsām ukṣṇāṃ jyāyasāṃ saṃpradānam
english: He who gives away all earthly desires gathered into one, and a milch-cow that yields every wish—rightly do such cows abound in streams of offerings to gods and ancestors; and greater still is the bestowal of the bulls among them.

sanskrit: na cāśiṣyāyāvratāyopakuryān; nāśraddadhānāya na vakrabuddhaye guhyo hy ayaṃ sarvalokasya dharmo; nemaṃ dharmaṃ yatra tatra prajalpet
english: One should not impart this to a non-pupil, to one without vows, nor to the unbelieving, nor to the crooked of mind; for this is the secret dharma of all the world, and one should not babble this dharma here and there.

sanskrit: santi loke śraddadhānā manuṣyāḥ; santi kṣudrā rākṣasā mānuṣeṣu yeṣāṃ dānaṃ dīyamānaṃ hy aniṣṭaṃ; nāstikyaṃ cāpy āśrayante hy apuṇyāḥ
english: There are believing men in the world, and there are mean ones, very demons among men, to whom the giving of a gift is hateful; the unholy take refuge even in disbelief.

sanskrit: bārhaspatyaṃ vākyam etan niśamya; ye rājāno gopradānāni kṛtvā lokān prāptāḥ puṇyaśīlāḥ suvṛttās; tān me rājan kīrtyamānān nibodha
english: Hearing this counsel of Bṛhaspati, those kings who, having made gifts of cows, attained the worlds—holy in conduct and of good ways—hear of them, O king, as I recount them.

sanskrit: uśīnaro viṣvagaśvo nṛgaś ca; bhagīratho viśruto yauvanāśvaḥ māndhātā vai mucukundaś ca rājā; bhūridyumno naiṣadhaḥ somakaś ca
english: Uśīnara, Viṣvagaśva, and Nṛga; Bhagīratha, and the renowned son of Yuvanāśva; Māndhātṛ indeed, and King Mucukunda; Bhūridyumna, the lord of Niṣadha, and Somaka—

sanskrit: purūravā bharataś cakravartī; yasyānvaye bhāratāḥ sarva eva tathā vīro dāśarathiś ca rāmo; ye cāpy anye viśrutāḥ kīrtimantaḥ
english: Purūravas, and Bharata the universal emperor, in whose line are all the Bhāratas; and the hero Rāma, son of Daśaratha; and whatever others renowned and glorious there were.

sanskrit: tathā rājā pṛthukarmā dilīpo; divaṃ prāpto gopradāne vidhijñaḥ yajñair dānais tapasā rājadharmair; māndhātābhūd gopradānaiś ca yuktaḥ
english: So too King Dilīpa of mighty deeds, knowing the ordinance of the gift of cows, attained heaven; and Māndhātṛ became great through sacrifices, gifts, austerity, the duties of kings, and through gifts of cows.

sanskrit: tasmāt pārtha tvam apīmāṃ mayoktāṃ; bārhaspatīṃ bhāratīṃ dhārayasva dvijāgryebhyaḥ saṃprayaccha pratīto; gāḥ puṇyā vai prāpya rājyaṃ kurūṇām
english: Therefore, O Pārtha, do you too hold fast to this teaching of Bṛhaspati that I have spoken; and gladly, having gained the kingdom of the Kurus, bestow holy cows upon the foremost of the twice-born.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā sarvaṃ kṛtavān dharmarājo; bhīṣmeṇokto vidhivad gopradāne sa māndhātur devadevopadiṣṭaṃ; samyag dharmaṃ dhārayām āsa rājā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: So the King of Righteousness did all this, as Bhīṣma had told him, duly in the gift of cows; that king rightly upheld the dharma of Māndhātṛ, which had been taught by the god of gods.

sanskrit: iti nṛpa satataṃ gavāṃ pradāne; yavaśakalān saha gomayaiḥ pibānaḥ kṣititalaśayanaḥ śikhī yatātmā; vṛṣa iva rājavṛṣas tadā babhūva
english: Thus, O king, ever intent upon the giving of cows, drinking barley-grains together with cow-dung, sleeping upon the bare ground, wearing the tuft, self-controlled—that bull among kings became then as a bull itself.

sanskrit: sa nṛpatir abhavat sadaiva tābhyaḥ; prayatamanā hy abhisaṃstuvaṃś ca gā vai nṛpadhuri ca na gām ayuṅkta bhūyas; turagavarair agamac ca yatra tatra
english: That king was ever devoted to them, with mind made pure, glorifying the cows; and he yoked no cow again to the burden of royal service, but went here and there with his choicest steeds.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā bhūyaḥ śāṃtanavaṃ nṛpa godāne vistaraṃ dhīmān papraccha vinayānvitaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira the wise, O king, full of humility, asked the son of Śaṃtanu yet further about the gift of cows in its fullness.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca gopradāne guṇān samyak punaḥ prabrūhi bhārata na hi tṛpyāmy ahaṃ vīra śṛṇvāno 'mṛtam īdṛśam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Tell me once more, O Bhārata, the merits in the gift of cows, fully; for I am not sated, O hero, listening to such nectar as this.

sanskrit: ity ukto dharmarājena tadā śāṃtanavo nṛpa samyag āha guṇāṃs tasmai gopradānasya kevalān
english: Thus addressed by the King of Righteousness, the son of Śaṃtanu, O king, then duly recounted to him the unmixed merits of the gift of cows.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca vatsalāṃ guṇasaṃpannāṃ taruṇīṃ vastrasaṃvṛtām dattvedṛśīṃ gāṃ viprāya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: Bhīṣma said: Giving to a brāhmaṇa such a cow—affectionate, endowed with good qualities, young, and draped with cloth—a man is freed from all his sins.

sanskrit: asuryā nāma te lokā gāṃ dattvā tatra gacchati pītodakāṃ jagdhatṛṇāṃ naṣṭadugdhāṃ nirindriyām
english: There are worlds called 'sunless'; into them one goes who gives a cow whose water is drunk dry, whose grass is eaten up, whose milk has failed, and whose powers are spent—

sanskrit: jarogrām upayuktārthāṃ jīrṇāṃ kūpam ivājalam dattvā tamaḥ praviśati dvijaṃ kleśena yojayet
english: —worn out with age, her usefulness already taken, decrepit like a waterless well; giving such a one, he enters darkness, for he would yoke the twice-born to mere trouble.

sanskrit: duṣṭā ruṣṭā vyādhitā durbalā vā; na dātavyā yāś ca mūlyair adattaiḥ kleśair vipraṃ yo 'phalaiḥ saṃyunakti; tasyāvīryāś cāphalāś caiva lokāḥ
english: A cow that is vicious, ill-tempered, diseased, or feeble, and those for which the price has not been paid, are not to be given; he who yokes a brāhmaṇa to troubles that bear no fruit—his worlds too shall be without vigour and without fruit.

sanskrit: balānvitāḥ śīlavayopapannāḥ; sarvāḥ praśaṃsanti sugandhavatyaḥ yathā hi gaṅgā saritāṃ variṣṭhā; tathārjunīnāṃ kapilā variṣṭhā
english: All praise cows that are strong, endowed with good temper and right age, and sweet of scent; for as the Gaṅgā is the best of rivers, so among the white cows the tawny one is the best.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kasmāt samāne bahulāpradāne; sadbhiḥ praśastaṃ kapilāpradānam viśeṣam icchāmi mahānubhāva; śrotuṃ samartho hi bhavān pravaktum
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When the gift of a many-coloured cow is the same, why is the gift of a tawny one extolled by the good? I wish to hear the distinction, O great-souled one; for you are able to declare it.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca vṛddhānāṃ bruvatāṃ tāta śrutaṃ me yat prabhāṣase vakṣyāmi tad aśeṣeṇa rohiṇyo nirmitā yathā
english: Bhīṣma said: What I have heard from the elders as they spoke, that, my son, of which you ask, I shall tell you in full—how the red cows were fashioned.

sanskrit: prajāḥ sṛjeti vyādiṣṭaḥ pūrvaṃ dakṣaḥ svayaṃbhuvā asṛjad vṛttim evāgre prajānāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: Commanded of old by the Self-existent, 'Create creatures,' Dakṣa first of all created their very sustenance, desiring the welfare of beings.

sanskrit: yathā hy amṛtam āśritya vartayanti divaukasaḥ tathā vṛttiṃ samāśritya vartayanti prajā vibho
english: For as the dwellers in heaven subsist depending on the nectar, even so do creatures subsist depending upon their sustenance, O mighty one.

sanskrit: acarebhyaś ca bhūtebhyaś carāḥ śreṣṭhās tato narāḥ brāhmaṇāś ca tataḥ śreṣṭhās teṣu yajñāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
english: Than motionless beings the moving are better, and than these, men; and than these, the brāhmaṇas are best; in them the sacrifices are established.

sanskrit: yajñair āpyāyate somaḥ sa ca goṣu pratiṣṭhitaḥ sarve devāḥ pramodante pūrvavṛttās tataḥ prajāḥ
english: By sacrifices the Soma is nourished, and that is established in the cows; all the gods rejoice, and thence creatures fare as of old.

sanskrit: etāny eva tu bhūtāni prākrośan vṛttikāṅkṣayā vṛttidaṃ cānvapadyanta tṛṣitāḥ pitṛmātṛvat
english: Now these very beings cried aloud in longing for sustenance, and athirst they came after the giver of sustenance as toward a father and mother.

sanskrit: itīdaṃ manasā gatvā prajāsargārtham ātmanaḥ prajāpatir balādhānam amṛtaṃ prāpibat tadā
english: Pondering this in his mind, Prajāpati then, for the sake of his own creation of beings, drank the nectar that bestows strength.

sanskrit: sa gatas tasya tṛptiṃ tu gandhaṃ surabhim udgiran dadarśodgārasaṃvṛttāṃ surabhiṃ mukhajāṃ sutām
english: Having come to the contentment thereof, belching forth a fragrant odour, he beheld Surabhi, the daughter born from his mouth, brought forth from his eructation.

sanskrit: sāsṛjat saurabheyīs tu surabhir lokamātaraḥ suvarṇavarṇāḥ kapilāḥ prajānāṃ vṛttidhenavaḥ
english: And Surabhi brought forth the daughters of Surabhi, the mothers of the world—tawny cows of golden hue, the milch-cows that are the sustenance of creatures.

sanskrit: tāsām amṛtavarṇānāṃ kṣarantīnāṃ samantataḥ babhūvāmṛtajaḥ phenaḥ sravantīnām ivormijaḥ
english: As those of nectar-hue flowed forth on every side, there arose from them a foam born of the nectar, even as the wave-born foam of streaming rivers.

sanskrit: sa vatsamukhavibhraṣṭo bhavasya bhuvi tiṣṭhataḥ śirasy avāpa tat kruddhaḥ sa tadodaikṣata prabhuḥ lalāṭaprabhavenākṣṇā rohiṇīḥ pradahann iva
english: That foam, fallen from the mouth of a calf, lighted upon the head of Bhava as he stood upon the earth; thereat the Lord, enraged, gazed upon the red cows with the eye sprung from his forehead, as though to burn them up.

sanskrit: tat tejas tu tato raudraṃ kapilā gā viśāṃ pate nānāvarṇatvam anayan meghān iva divākaraḥ
english: That fierce splendour, O lord of peoples, brought the tawny cows to many-coloured hues, as the sun colours the clouds.

sanskrit: yās tu tasmād apakramya somam evābhisaṃśritāḥ yathotpannāḥ svavarṇasthās tā nītā nānyavarṇatām
english: But those that drew away from it and took refuge in the Soma, abiding in their own hue as they were born, were not brought to any other colour.

sanskrit: atha kruddhaṃ mahādevaṃ prajāpatir abhāṣata amṛtenāvasiktas tvaṃ nocchiṣṭaṃ vidyate gavām
english: Then Prajāpati spoke to the angry Mahādeva: 'You have been besprinkled with nectar; there is no defilement among the cows.

sanskrit: yathā hy amṛtam ādāya somo viṣyandate punaḥ tathā kṣīraṃ kṣaranty etā rohiṇyo 'mṛtasaṃbhavāḥ
english: For as the Soma, having taken up the nectar, flows forth again, so do these red cows, sprung from the nectar, pour forth their milk.

sanskrit: na duṣyaty anilo nāgnir na suvarṇaṃ na codadhiḥ nāmṛtenāmṛtaṃ pītaṃ vatsapītā na vatsalā
english: The wind is not defiled, nor fire, nor gold, nor the ocean; nectar drunk by nectar is no defilement, and the loving cow, drunk of by her calf, is not made impure.

sanskrit: imāṃl lokān bhariṣyanti haviṣā prasnavena ca āsām aiśvaryam aśnīhi sarvāmṛtamayaṃ śubham
english: These cows shall sustain the worlds with their oblation and their milk; partake of their sovereignty, auspicious and made wholly of nectar.'

sanskrit: vṛṣabhaṃ ca dadau tasmai saha tābhiḥ prajāpatiḥ prasādayām āsa manas tena rudrasya bhārata
english: And Prajāpati gave him a bull together with those cows, and by that he won over the mind of Rudra, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: prītaś cāpi mahādevaś cakāra vṛṣabhaṃ tadā dhvajaṃ ca vāhanaṃ caiva tasmāt sa vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ
english: And Mahādeva, well pleased, then made the bull both his banner and his mount; therefore is he the Bull-bannered one.
